note: Ideas tested leave-one-tournament-out and rejected. delta and ci_* are the change in combined held-out multiclass Brier vs the relevant baseline; NEGATIVE = lower Brier = would have helped. null = no single point estimate or no block-bootstrap CI published (a qualitative or noise-floor result). Curated by hand from the README negative-findings sections; A4 is from research/a4_probe.py.

items.reason: a per-confederation-pair goal-difference residual added to inter-confederation matchups
items.note: Improved Brier by -0.016 on the bare goal model, but collapses to -0.005 (CI spans zero, one tournament reverses) on the production model, where rich squads already cluster in strong confederations and the value prior absorbs about two-thirds of the effect. Phase 1 re-gated it on a 2,180-match surface (five World Cups plus continental finals), where it is not merely absorbed but actively harmful: 0.0020 worse at scale 0.5 and 0.0047 at scale 1.0, worst on the 494 inter-confederation matches it targets (0.0089 then 0.0209 worse). See research/phase1_results.md.

items.reason: a leave-one-tournament-out map that sharpens the favourite's probability
items.note: Cut reliability but traded away resolution and reversed sign on one tournament; the 95% CI grazes zero. The temperature lesson a third time.

items.reason: a form coefficient well above the shipped 0.20, found by a leave-one-tournament-out sweep
items.note: Lowers pooled Brier from 0.5441 to 0.5393 on the 320 World Cup matches and improves four of five, but 2022 regresses and the paired CI grazes zero. Phase 1 re-gated it on a 2,180-match surface, where the World Cup gain reverses: lambda 0.60 is 0.0064 worse than the shipped 0.20 (paired 95% interval [+0.0026, +0.0103], entirely on the worse side), and 0.20 is the surface optimum. The 320-match optimum was overfitting. See research/phase1_results.md.

items.reason: the actual 23-man rosters valued in place of the top-26-by-value proxy
items.note: Proxy 0.5605 vs real squads 0.5631 on the three tournaments with adequate valuation coverage (2014/18/22). The standardised log-value prior already tracks the real squad (correlation ~0.99), so the swap barely moves the model.

items.reason: a longer time-decay half-life on the ratings fit
items.note: 0.595 vs 0.598 pooled, inside the +-0.015 to 0.020 block-bootstrap noise floor over five tournaments.

items.reason: down-weight friendlies and up-weight finals in the ratings fit
items.note: 0.5454 vs the 0.5441 baseline; only two of five tournaments improve and resolution fell rather than rose, the opposite of the intended effect.

items.reason: a shared Poisson component on top of Dixon-Coles
items.note: 0.573 vs 0.574 on the plain goal model; a negligible move well inside noise.

items.reason: a learned weight between the two engines
items.note: +0.0007 worse than plain Elo (baseline here is Elo). Leave-one-tournament-out drives the weight to near-pure Elo in every fold and the CI never favours the blend.

items.reason: a single multiplier applied to every draw probability
items.note: The factor reverts to 1.0 every fold; scaling all draws uniformly just flows back to both sides. The asymmetric version of this idea became the shipped draw-transfer.

items.reason: the actual starting XI valued as-of kickoff (StatsBomb, 2018 and 2022)
items.note: Only a weak residual correlation of 0.06 that did not transfer between tournaments and cost resolution out of sample.
At most a noise-floor Brier change, with no certifiable lift in resolution.

items.reason: a global confidence rescale of the probabilities
items.note: Sharpened in-sample but made held-out 2022 worse on every metric; the calibration direction is not stable across tournaments, so none is applied.

items.reason: days of rest between matches as a feature
shrink every team's rating toward average each year
items.note: Never helped at any strength; national-team strength is more persistent than folklore suggests.

items.reason: dock a team's value prior for players known unavailable before kickoff
items.note: On the leakage-clean 2018 and 2022 absences the depleted teams overperformed the model (France lost Benzema, Pogba and Kante and still reached the final), so a cut points the wrong way: net -0.33 points across 21 depleted-team matches. Not pursued to a full gate.
